clarifyingQuestions: Should duplicate text be detected exactly, normalized, or semantically?
Should final output preserve rank order or original document order?
Should per-document limits be hard or only a diversity penalty?
followUps: Use maximal marginal relevance to balance relevance and similarity to already selected chunks.
Guarantee at least one chunk from each high-scoring document.
Group neighboring chunks after selection for better answer context.
followUpGuide: For MMR, score each candidate by relevance minus similarity to already selected chunks. That trades a hard duplicate skip for a diversity-aware rank.
For document coverage, reserve slots for top documents first, then fill remaining slots globally.
For neighboring chunks, select anchor chunks first, then expand around anchors while keeping the total token budget under control.
complexityAnalysis: - Base contract: sort all n candidates by (-score, id), then greedily filter. Let L be the total text length normalized during the scan and S the total length of retained normalized strings. Time: O(n log n + L) expected with hash sets, treating ID comparisons as constant time. Space: O(n + d + S) plus one temporary normalized string, where d is the number of encountered documents. A heap containing only the raw top k can underfill after filtering.
- Follow-up: heap of size k only when there is no text dedupe or per-doc cap. Time: O(n log k). Space: O(k).
- Follow-up: MMR or soft diversity penalties after ranking. Time depends on similarity work; reserve heap/MMR notes for those variants only.
solutionGuide: Sort candidates by `(-score, id)`. Track normalized text and counts per doc as you select.

Normalize text with `' '.join(text.lower().split())`. Python's [`str.split` without a separator](https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str.split) collapses whitespace runs and removes leading/trailing whitespace. This exercise compares lowercase strings; semantic similarity and Unicode casefolding require separate handling.
